title: Rain lane / navigation

actual_tool_inputs.prompt:
Transform this isolated character study into a ZOOMED-OUT PLAYABLE 2D GAME LEVEL VIEW. Replace the ENTIRE old composition and background with a continuous navigable ground map. Keep the exact S49 knight design, helmet, costume, weapon, shield and head/body ratio, but SCALE THE WHOLE KNIGHT DOWN to ONE-TENTH of canvas height. He is a SMALL IN-WORLD ACTOR. No giant foreground hero. ONE player only. All other humans are UNARMORED and equally tiny with oversized heads and tiny short squat bodies. Match their total figure height to the knight, not to his torso.

Explore a confined diagonal village lane after rain. Guarin waits beside a shallow muddy well while two afflicted neighbors obstruct a branching path between low limestone cottages. A modest round-arched church lies far up the lane. Use an asymmetric map-like arrangement, wet ash-grey daylight, puddles and quiet spatial tension; no battle pose. The navigable ground and corners should feel like a real playable route.

The map fills EVERY canvas edge. View from a HIGH elevated orthographic camera about 45 degrees above the ground, showing floor/ground and roof planes. NO horizon, NO scenic eye-level perspective, NO paper margins, NO poster or miniature diorama. Show plenty of navigable ground around every actor. Player and neighbors each occupy ONLY one-tenth of image height and share the same ground plane. Draw ALL terrain, buildings, people and creatures in the EXACT supplied character's medium: dirty gouache/watercolor-like brush washes and scraped pigment, irregular drawn edges, muted grey-brown and faded wine; extend the attached painting medium to every background object and actor. Common desaturated charcoal/mud/faded-wine palette and shared local light; no bright pasted-on character layer. Fictional rural Rivoire, Royans/Isère, 1101, modest Romanesque forms and weary poor neighbors. Only 2D drawn game art; no 3D rendering, photorealism, collage, reference inset, captions or new character design. For S01 use the full-body knight and keep the original nasal helmet and face, ignoring the separate portrait. Preserve this exact original character and build a game WORLD around him; the gameplay camera and actor scale must change from the portrait source.

visual_assessment.assessor: Parent assistant after viewing the actual image and exact character source
visual_assessment.observations: The exact S49 helmet, mail, scarf, shield and painting are recognizable; palette and light are shared.
visual_assessment.limitations: Held back as a gameplay solution: low camera, large illustration-scale figures, longer-bodied neighbors and an extra villager. The v02 prompt removes the duplicate helmeted neighbor seen in v01.
